one_liner: FIDENTIS uses 3D printing to automate production of dental prostheses with precious-metal components and secured €1.62 million in research-transfer funding.

top_signals.signal: Received €1.62 million through the EXIST Transfer of Research program in July 2024.
Named a winner or finalist in the 2025 BayStartUP Bavarian Business Plan Competition.
The Fraunhofer IGCV spin-off uses laser powder bed fusion to process two alloys in a single component.

team: Dr. Max Horn (CEO) holds a PhD. He and Timo Schröder (CTO and technology lead) are listed as technical founders. Johannes Lauer leads commercial activities, and Lukas Langer is COO and production lead.
why_early: The documented funding came through EXIST; whether a priced round has taken place is unknown.
devils_advocate_risks: Reliability and scalability at mass-production volumes remain to be validated.
Adoption by dental professionals and patients is uncertain.
next_step: The HTGF Life Sciences & Chemistry team should ask: What share of prostheses in your largest production run met your quality specifications?
